title: Postman collection export: literal credential in an auth attribute entry
summary: A synthetic Postman Collection v2.1 export whose collection-level auth is type apikey. The apikey array holds three entries, each an object with key, value and type properties: one names the header X-API-Key, one is the entry whose key is the string value and whose value property holds a synthetic PMAK-shaped literal, one names where the key goes (header). A synthetic collection id sits in info.
rationale: In this layout the label of the credential is not a JSON property name. Each attribute is an object {key, value, type}: the word value is a string held by the property key, and the secret is the string held by the property value in the same object. A reader that pairs a property name with its string sees only key and value, and one that looks at nearby words sees the header name X-API-Key. The credential is recognised by its own grammar, so the expected span is the credential string only, not the entry and not the sibling attributes. The collection id beside it is an identifier by the schema's own description and carries no span.

expectation.rationale: Flag one span: the PMAK-shaped string in the value attribute entry. The span rests on the family grammar, for which two artifacts by different maintainers are consistent with PMAK- followed by 24 hex characters, a hyphen and 34 hex characters. The export layout facts come from Postman's own schema and runtime source: an auth block holds an array of key/value/type entries, and the apikey type reads the attributes key, value and in. They say where the value sits, not that a value is confidential, so they are not the basis of the span. Preconditions: the input is the exported JSON text read as UTF-8; no JSON decoding, key-value pairing or variable resolution is assumed, and any such capability is the consumer's claim to make. Silence on the collection id is stated by omission only: no span is expected there, and whether a real collection id is confidential is not established by these sources.

sources.supports: The postman-api-token rule matches PMAK- followed by 24 hexadecimal characters, a hyphen and 34 hexadecimal characters.
The Postman detector pattern matches PMAK- followed by 59 characters, consistent with the 24 + hyphen + 34 split but wider in alphabet.
An auth object holds, per auth type, an array of attribute objects with key, value and type properties; an auth attribute is described with username and password as the Basic attributes.
The apikey authorizer reads the attributes key, value and in, where in is header or query.
The bearer authorizer reads its credential from the auth attribute named token.
info._postman_id is described as the unique value that identifies a collection.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04; no scanner was run and no scanner output was consulted (the two rule files are pinned text artifacts cited for grammar consistency only). Origin: evidence-derived from the Postman schema and SDK layouts, synthetic value.
